justification.conditionality: The model cost is time-discounted over a fixed horizon and restricted to land near natural forest, the Uganda figure is a single table entry with no price year, and the Brazilian figure is upper-middle income and a grouped value for several low-input approaches; only the Uganda figure enters the class, and none includes the opportunity cost of land.

effect_mechanism: In a plantation trial on pasture in La Chontalpa, Tabasco, Mexico, semi-mechanised planting cost US$178/ha against US$217/ha by hand [ev_project_cost_keyes97_1, ev_project_cost_keyes97_2]; plantation establishment in the Masoala corridors of Madagascar is listed at 279 dollars per hectare [ev_project_cost_wri17_3]; and modelled implementation cost for plantations across low- and middle-income countries has a median of US$3,729/ha, inclusive of replanting after harvest cycles, against US$140/ha for natural regeneration [ev_project_cost_busch24_2].
conditionality: The cost class is set by the Madagascar entry, the only one in the low-income band; the Mexican and modelled figures sit outside it. The Mexican figures are historical field costs for establishment and first-year maintenance that exclude donated seedlings, and the modelled median counts replanting over harvest cycles, with an interdecile range of US$1,530–11,675/ha [ev_project_cost_busch24_2]. These are production-plantation costs, not the cost of restoration toward a natural baseline. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

effect_mechanism: Natural regeneration lowers cost by letting forests grow back on their own or with low-cost assistance, cited at US$12-3,880/ha against US$105-25,830/ha for restoration projects, and is often more effective than full tree planting in long-term success [ev_project_cost_williams24_1]; European guidelines likewise note its lower cost and locally adapted genetic material [ev_project_cost_stanturf26_1]. In a mulching experiment in tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, polyethylene mulch cut the cost of each established plant, including nursery costs, from 18.00 USD on bare soil to 2.45 USD, because 92 of 180 plants established against 10 of 180 without mulch [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. Decentralised administration of Van Panchayat forests in India is associated with costs approximately 1/13th of those under state administration [ev_project_cost_samii14_1].
conditionality: The European statement is an expert assertion that also notes limits in species composition, and the cost comparison is a cited range without price year. Organic mulches cut cost per established plant less, to 12.50 USD with alfalfa straw and 13.33 USD with leaf litter, and the result comes from a single experiment at one site [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]; the Van Panchayat cost figure is cited in a systematic review and concerns administering existing forest [ev_project_cost_samii14_1].

justification.pool_note: This row draws on 3 evidence unit(s) from 3 source(s); the weighting counts sources, not units, so several findings from one paper do not multiply its say.
justification.mechanism: Recurrent costs are compiler-entered annual maintenance costs per hectare on WOCAT sheets for the community forest package in India and the protected learning site in Afghanistan [ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance]. A payment scheme in Costa Rica is estimated to spend between $255 and $382 per year per hectare of additional forest [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
justification.conditionality: The two compiler entries differ widely, the Indian one is converted from local currency and spread over mixed plantation and nursery areas, and neither sheet itemises maintenance tasks [ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance]. The Costa Rican figure is payment spending per hectare of additional forest rather than a maintenance cost, from an upper-middle-income country, and is cited in a systematic review [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
